kinds.golden: two per tag, echoes the wording — a floor, not a gate
kinds.pair: one quote each side of a sibling seam
kinds.oos: everyday uses of tag words; must stay under 0.4
kinds.trap: a must-not case for one tag

quotes.text: Oh nice, the 'Split bill' button's right there at the bottom of the receipt, exactly where I'd look.
It's obvious what to do here — there's a big 'Start scan' and nothing else competing with it.
Wait, you can swipe left on a message to reply to it? I've had this phone two years.
Where's the option to export? ... oh, it's under the three dots, under 'More', under 'Advanced'. Who'd find that?
I'm just going to tap around and see what these icons do.
Let me try long-pressing this... nope. What if I drag it? Ah, something happened.
The first week I had the watch I kept accidentally triggering the SOS thing, but once you learn the button combos it's fine.
When I first opened it I had no idea what any of the tabs were for, took me a couple of sessions to get my bearings.
Good, it went green and said 'Saved' straight away, so I know it took.
As soon as I tapped pay the little tick came up and my phone buzzed. Clear.
I pressed submit and... is it doing anything? There's no spinner. Should I press it again?
It just sat there for ages after I hit 'Book', I genuinely thought it had crashed, then the confirmation popped up.
It says 'Error 0x80004005'. What am I supposed to do with that?
It flashed something and went back to the list — did it save? Did it delete? I honestly can't tell.
I do like that it asked 'Are you sure?' before it wiped the playlist.
It just deleted the whole folder with no 'are you sure'. I wish it had checked first.
I'm assuming the cloud icon means it's backed up somewhere, and the phone icon means it's only on this device.
So my theory is the thermostat learns from when I turn it down, and it'll start doing that itself.
Oh I see, it actually sorts by the date you added it, not the date it was taken. That explains the order.
Turns out the 'favourites' are shared across all the profiles in the house, it's not per person.
Hang on, I archived it, why has it disappeared completely? I thought archive meant 'put it away', not 'delete'.
I expected 'Undo' to bring back the last thing I deleted, but it undid the rename instead. That's not what I meant.
In every other app pull-down refreshes, so that's what I did.
I'm so used to Gmail that I keep hitting 'e' to archive, and here that does nothing.
The dial actually turns, so I turned it — it's a physical knob, it does what a knob does.
It's a proper slider, you can grab it and drag it, there's no question about what it's for.
This looks like I should be able to drag it up... I think. Let me try.
That tile seems tappable, it's got a shadow like a card. I'll assume it opens something.
I've been tapping this banner for ten seconds — it looks like a button but it's just a picture.
That underlined blue text, I clicked it, nothing. It's not a link, it's just styled like one.
How was I supposed to know you could tap the header to sort? There's nothing to suggest it.
There's no handle or anything on this panel — I only found out it slides because I brushed it by accident.
Turn the ring right, volume goes up. Obviously.
The left stick moves left, the right stick moves right — you don't even have to think about it.
Four identical buttons in a row and the lights are in a square. I always get the wrong one.
Why does the top switch control the bottom light? I have to memorise it every time.
The seat controls are shaped like the seat, so you push the bit you want to move. Lovely.
The little map of the rooms matches where the rooms actually are, so I just tap the room I'm in.
All the account stuff is together, and all the money-moving stuff is together. Sensible.
The steps go top to bottom in the order you'd actually do them. That's well organised.
The 'Pay' button's greyed out until I fill in the amount, so I can't send nothing by accident.
The plug only goes in one way, so you can't get it wrong.
I'd never put my full name in a public username, that's just not done where I'm from.
You're supposed to wait to be seated, so I didn't just tap 'take table 4' even though I could have.
There's only one slot labelled 'Card', so obviously that's where the card goes.
quotes.note: arguably a signifier; codebook's own example shape

quotes.text: The field says 'Postcode' so I'm not going to put my phone number in it, it wouldn't make sense.
There are three cables and three sockets left, so by elimination that one goes there.
It wouldn't make sense to pick a delivery slot before I've entered an address, so I'll do the address first.
Oops, I hit 'Delete' instead of 'Edit', they're right next to each other.
Fat-fingered the 9 instead of the 8. My fault, but the keys are tiny.
Wait, where was I... did I already add the coupon or not?
I forgot to attach the file again. Every single time.
I double-tapped to zoom like you do in Maps, but here double-tap 'likes' the photo. Sent a like to my ex.
I thought you had to save before leaving, like in the old version, so I hit Save and it created a duplicate.
I don't know what any of these settings mean — 'bitrate', 'codec' — I'm just guessing.
I have no idea how to get it to do the thing. I'm just pressing things and hoping.
I pushed, it didn't open. There's a handle so I pulled. Turns out you push — the handle is lying to me.
The knobs are in a straight line but the burners are in a square, so I keep heating the wrong pan.
I couldn't work out how to make the shower hot — one knob does temperature AND pressure and there's no marking at all.
You can't start it unless your foot's on the brake, which annoyed me at first but it's stopped me lurching forward.
Six switches in a row by the door and I still don't know which one does the hall light.
I typed my message and it went into the search box instead, because I was in the wrong mode and nothing told me.
quotes.note: mode error — no home in this codebook

quotes.text: I meant to go to the settings but I ended up on the home screen — my thumb just does the usual thing out of habit.
I don't have to remember the wifi password, it's on the sticker on the router.
quotes.note: knowledge in the world — no home; expect low confidence

quotes.text: I pressed the button on the hob and I genuinely can't tell whether it's on now.
It's a beautiful colour, I love the green of it.
quotes.note: visceral reaction — Norman ch.2, not in codebook; expect low confidence

quotes.text: I got some really useful feedback from my manager on the presentation.
My dad was a plumber so I grew up knowing how boilers work.
We normally do the big shop on a Saturday and I take the kids.
I've been a nurse for twelve years, mostly in A&E.
The pandemic changed everything about how we worked as a team.
I love hiking, I'm out most weekends if the weather's decent.
My mental model of the housing market is basically that it's a bubble.
Honestly I'm just tired today, it's been a long week.
I usually explore a new city on foot the first day, no map.
The train was delayed forty minutes so I missed the connection.
I made a mistake choosing that university, in hindsight.
You're supposed to bring a gift when you visit someone's house, that's just manners.
There's a little grey bar at the bottom, I assumed it was just decoration, turns out you drag it up and that's where the filters live.
I've been through every menu. There are no filters anywhere. ... Oh. It's a two-finger swipe. Nobody on earth would find that.
I tapped it and it went a bit darker for a second and then, nothing, so, has it added it? I'll check the basket later I suppose.
It's thinking. Still thinking. Okay. I'll give it a minute.
I reckon it's saving as I go, it looks like the sort of thing that would, so I'm not going to bother looking for a save button.
Ah right, so it's doing it per line, not per document. Okay. That's why only that bit changed.
No, that's — I set it to Tuesday and it's booked Thursday. What? Why would it do that?
I'm swiping from the left to go back, that's just what you do on a phone. Yep, there we go.
I swiped to go back and it deleted the row. On my phone swiping is back. Well that's gone then.
You can tell that rotates, it's got that ridged edge you get on a dial, and yeah, it does.
I'd guess this spins? It's round. Might just be a badge though. Let's see.
Up is louder. That's how it should be, I don't want to think about it.
The four buttons are laid out the same way as the four zones on the screen, so top-left does top-left. Good.
Personal details, then payment, then confirm. That's the sensible order, it's how I'd have put it.
It won't take the form until the date's in. Fine, it's not letting me skip it.
Well there's only one section I haven't filled in, so it must be that one that's stopping it.
The red one's obviously stop and the green one's go, I didn't even read them.
quotes.note: colour convention = cultural in Norman; codebook says semantic

quotes.text: The 'to' address obviously goes in the recipient box, that's what recipient means.
I went to type my postcode and I'd typed it in the city box, I was looking at the other screen.
Got to the end and it says no delivery date. Oh — I never picked one, did I. Skipped straight past it.
I assumed 'archive' worked like it does in Outlook so I archived the lot, and now they've vanished from the app entirely.
I don't really know what a 'workspace' is versus a 'project', so I've made one of each and I'm hoping one of them's right.
It made me type DELETE in capitals before it would go ahead. Bit much, but I get why.
Not sure what this one does. Let's find out.
I've pressed everything on this screen and none of it's what I want and I still don't get what the screen is for.
The checkout button's massive and yellow, can't miss it.
Yep, it's in. Little number on the bag went to one.

Right so I want a bed, a double, um, let me — beds... here we go, beds and mattresses, and then it's giving me bed frames, mattresses, um, I don't want a mattress yet, bed frames. And now there's like forty of them, is there a — can I do it by price, I'd have thought there'd be a sort thing, um... there it is, top right, tiny.
Okay, add to bag. Did it — hm. I'll press it again. Oh no, now I've got two. Great.
I always think the heart's for the basket. It's not, it's a wishlist. I do this every single time on every site.
quotes.note: repeated wrong rule about an icon

quotes.text: So it's asking me for my postcode before it'll show me stock, I suppose that's because it's per store, yeah, that makes sense actually.
Hmm. 'Click and collect' and 'Collect from store'. What's the difference? Are those the same thing?
quotes.note: no clean home — two labels that don't discriminate

quotes.text: The filters are down the left and the results are on the right, and when I tick a colour the pictures — yeah, they all go white. Lovely.
Why is 'remove' right next to 'save for later'? I've just binned the thing I wanted to keep. Fine. Back it goes.
I'm going to guess that little house takes me home, it usually does.
The page has gone completely white. Is it loading? Is it broken? Is it me?
Oh, it's remembered my basket from last week. I didn't expect that. That's nice.
You know what, I'd expected it to say 'thanks, your order's on its way' or something at the end. It just went back to the homepage and I'm sat here going, did that go through?
It won't let me put more than nine in the basket, which, fair enough, who needs ten wardrobes.
I keep pressing the picture expecting it to get bigger and it doesn't.
My wife would have gone straight to the app. I never use the app, I go on the laptop.
That's a lot of steps just to change the delivery address. Back, back, back, edit, save, then it makes you re-confirm the whole thing.
quotes.note: no efficiency tag in Norman; measure where it lands
